newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil down on commercial selling, meal mixed.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil down on commercial selling, meal mixed.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures were lower at midsession Tuesday, under pressure from commercial selling and technical weakness, while soymeal was mixed, floor traders said.
"The real story down there today is the technical give-up in oil," said one Chicago analyst.
Profit-taking on the soyoil/soymeal spread pushed soymeal futures away from session lows, traders said. May soymeal fell as much as $3.00 per ton early before recovering to show only modest losses.
In early trading, ADM sold 300 lots May soyoil and Cargill sold 100 lots of July, pit traders said.
Talk that China was looking to buy an unspecified quantity of South American soymeal was said to limit gains in CBOT futures, traders said.
However, one trader with clients in South America said there had been no recent indications of Chinese buying.
"I really don't think they're (China) going to chase the market right now," said the trader. "They're going to wait for prices to move lower."
At 1127 CDT, soymeal was up $2.00 to down $0.50 per ton, with July up $0.20 at $268.00 per ton. Soyoil futures were down 0.30 to 0.21, with July down 0.25 at 24.84 cents per lb.
